title: Shyam Sunder Goswami v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Abhinava Upadhya, J.; Shamim Ahmed, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; EE to consider objection in one month; coercive action stayed.
headnote: On a challenge that inspection was contrary to clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and that a theft/final assessment had been made without considering the consumer's objection to the Executive Engineer, the Division Bench disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to consider that objection within one month and pass an appropriate order in accordance with law, staying coercive action on the demand dated 26 November 2019 for that period. Whether clause 8.1 non-compliance vitiated the assessment, and whether a section 127 appeal barred the writ, were not decided.
facts: The petitioner challenged inspection of his premises as contrary to clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The department alleged theft and use of a domestic connection for a school, and made a final assessment with a demand dated 26 November 2019, said to be appealable under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. He had already represented to the Executive Engineer; the final order issued without considering that objection. Licensee's counsel did not dispute that inspection was not in accordance with clause 8.1.

holding_units.topic: unconsidered objection to theft assessment after clause 8.1 inspection
holding_units.holding: Where the consumer has already filed an objection before the Executive Engineer against a theft or final assessment and that objection has not been considered, the writ may be disposed of by directing the Executive Engineer to consider the objection within a stipulated period and pass an appropriate order in accordance with law, staying coercive action on the demand for that period, without deciding the clause 8.1 inspection challenge on merits or relegating the consumer to a section 127 appeal.

principle_tags.application: Inspection was alleged, and not disputed by the licensee, to have been conducted contrary to clause 8.1. The Court did not quash the assessment on that ground; it directed the Executive Engineer to consider the consumer's pending objection in accordance with law and stayed coercive recovery for one month.

not_decided.point: Whether inspection contrary to clause 8.1 vitiates the final theft assessment
not_decided.note: Licensee's counsel did not dispute that inspection was not in accordance with clause 8.1, but the Court did not quash the assessment on that ground.

not_decided.point: Whether the final assessment is appealable under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 so as to bar the writ
not_decided.note: The licensee submitted that the assessment was appealable under section 127; the Court did not relegate the petitioner to that appeal.
